questions.prompt: A Standard App Service app has automatic backups. It writes business documents to a custom-mounted Azure Files share. Recovery must restore both the app and those documents after accidental deletion. Which protection plan covers the separately stored documents?

options.text: Keep app backups and separately protect and test restoration of the Azure Files share.
options.explanation: Custom-mounted storage is excluded from App Service backups. Separate share protection and restore procedures cover the business documents.

options.text: Keep automatic app backups and use an app restore to recover the mounted-share documents.
options.explanation: Automatic app backups exclude custom-mounted Azure storage, so their app recovery points do not contain these documents.

options.text: Replace automatic app backups with custom app backups and recover the share from their ZIP files.
options.explanation: Custom app backups retain the same custom-mounted-storage exclusion; changing app backup type does not add the external documents.

options.text: Keep app backups and restore the storage mount configuration to recover the share documents.
options.explanation: Restoring a connection or mount configuration does not restore the external share content excluded from the app backup.

questions.prompt: A production web app on a Standard App Service plan is serving users. You must demonstrate that an app backup produces a working application before replacing production content. Production must keep serving during the test. A disposable staging slot and isolated test dependencies are available. Which recovery test meets these requirements?

options.text: Restore into the staging slot and test the recovered app against the isolated dependencies.
options.explanation: App Service stops the restore target, so using the staging slot preserves the production endpoint while functional checks establish recovery evidence.

options.text: Restore over production and test it after the restore completes.
options.explanation: An in-place restore stops and overwrites the production target, violating the requirement to keep it serving during the test.

options.text: Inspect the backup status and timestamp, then approve production replacement without restoring.
options.explanation: Job metadata does not demonstrate that the recovered application starts and works with its required dependencies.

options.text: Restore into staging and check only the recovered file count before approving replacement.
options.explanation: File presence alone does not establish working application behavior or successful access to the required test dependencies.

questions.prompt: In October 2026, you design a new App Service recovery setup with Azure SQL. Which database backup approach follows current Microsoft guidance?

options.text: Use Azure SQL native backup and restore alongside app protection.
options.explanation: Microsoft recommends native database tools, and new linked SQL backup configurations were removed in April 2026.

options.text: Depend on creating a new App Service linked SQL backup configuration.
options.explanation: The documented removal schedule has already removed this option for new configurations.

options.text: Assume automatic App Service backups include the SQL database.
options.explanation: Automatic backups do not include linked databases.

options.text: Use a deployment-slot swap as the only database backup.
options.explanation: A slot swap does not create a recoverable database backup.
